content.title: Tennessee vs Iowa State final score, highlights: Vols advance to Elite 8
content.text: Updated March 28, 2026, 4:24 p.m. ETCHICAGO — Iowa State basketball's quarter-century Elite Eight drought will continue for at least another year.The No. 2 seed Cyclones in the Midwest Region were knocked out of the NCAA Tournament in Friday, March 27's Sweet 16 loss to No. 6 Tennessee 76-62 at the United Center. Meanwhile, Tennessee is headed for its third straight Elite Eight appearance.Playing without All-American Joshua Jefferson (ankle), the Cyclones struggled to get much going offensively and couldn't keep up on the board against the Vols, who entered as the No. 1 offensive rebounding team.Tennessee won the rebounding battle 43-22 for the game, which included 16 offensive rebounds leading to 14 second-chance points.Nate Ament led the Vols with 18 points, four rebounds and three assists, while Ja'Kobi Gillespie added 16 points. Felix Okpara (12 points and 10 rebounds) and Jaylen Carey (11 points and 10 rebounds) each recorded double-doubles.The Vols won despite 17 turnovers.Nate Heise finished with 18 points, but scored just four points in the second half. Meanwhile, leading scorer Milan Momcilovic was limited to 6 points on 2-of-8 shooting. Tamin Lipsey also added 18 points.Tennessee advances to Sunday, March 29's Elite Eight, where it will play Michigan.USA TODAY brought you updates and highlights from Tennessee's Sweet 16 win over Iowa State. Catch up here:Tennessee vs Iowa State scoreTEAMS1H2HFTennessee344276Iowa State332962 Iowa State vs Tennessee highlights Final: Tennessee 76, Iowa State 62Tennessee is advancing to the Elite Eight with a 76-62 win over Iowa State in the Sweet 16 on Friday. The Vols outscored the Cyclones 42-29 in the second half to advance.Tennessee will make its third straight trip to the Elite Eight, where it will face No. 1 seed Michigan. The Vols have never advanced to the Final Four. Tennessee leads Iowa State by 10 at final media timeoutIt's 68-58 Tennessee with 3:00 left in the game, with a chance to advance to the Sweet 16 to play Michigan on Sunday.The Cyclones are struggling from the free-throw line, shooting 8-of-16 (50%) in the second half. Nate Heise will shoot a pair out of the media timeout. Tennessee leads Iowa State by 12At the under-8 media timeout, Tennessee leads Iowa State 61-49 with 7:48 left in the game. Both teams are in the bonus, so that means all fouls will result in free throws the rest of the way. Tennessee pushes lead to 13 points in second halfTennessee is beginning to pull away with a 7-0 run to push its lead to 54-41 with 12:57 left in the game. The Vols are outrebounding the Cyclones 28-11, including 6-to-1 since the intermission. Tennessee holds 7-point lead at first media timeoutTennessee leads 46-39 at the under-16 media timeout with 15:54 left in the game. The Vols are doubling up the Cyclones 12-6 in the second half.Nate Ament is up to 12 points to lead Tennessee, while Felix Okpara has 10. Nate Heise leads ISU with 14 points and Tamin Lipsey has 11. Second half of Iowa State-Tennessee Sweet 16 underwayThe second half of the Sweet 16 matchup between Iowa State and Tennessee is underway in Chicago. The Vols hold a 34-33 lead at the intermission.The largest lead for either side was just five points in the first half. There were four ties and five lead changes. Outside of Heise, the Cyclones are shooting 7-of-19 from the field in the first half. Killyan Toure heads to locker roomWith 51.2 seconds left in the first half, Iowa State starting guard Killyan Toure heads to the locker room. It's unclear what his injury was or when it happened. He had a behind-the-back to Tamin Lipsey on a fast break to give the Cyclones a 33-32 lead one possession before leaving. Tennessee continues to lead Iowa StateAt the final media timeout of the half, it's Tennessee leading Iowa State 30-26. The Vols have makes on six straight field goal attempts, with four different players sitting at least six points.Nate Heise leads all scorers with 11 points. Tennessee jumps ahead of Iowa StateTennessee holds a 22-19 lead the under-8 media timeout with 6:36 left in the first half. The Vols have makes on four of their last five shots to take their largest lead of the game. Iowa State-Tennessee locked in defensive struggleIowa State leads Tennessee 13-11 with 11:53 left in the first half at the second media timeout. The two teams have combined to shoot 9-of-26 (35%) from the field in the first 8-plus minutes.The Vols have seven offensive rebounds, but just two second-chance points so far. Iowa State leads Tennessee earlyAt the first media timeout, Tennessee is struggling to find the basket due to Iowa's defense. The Cyclones lead 8-4 with 15:39 left in the first half.Nate Heise has five points to lead all scorers, with three free throws knocked down already. The Vols are shooting 2-of-10 from the field. How to watch, streaming infoThe game is airing on TBS/truTV, streaming via Sling TV.Iowa State vs Tennessee prediction, odds∎ Eugene Rapay, Des Moines Register: Iowa State 74, Tennessee 68With or without Joshua Jefferson, Iowa State still has the pieces and tools to win. Jefferson's absence may create for a more uphill battle in the paint or on the glass, but the Cyclones' level of defensive disruption has only risen since the postseason tipped off. Creating turnovers will be the key, and Iowa State has already shown that it can weather cold-shooting stretches or adverse situations when it doubles down on defense. The Cyclones will need to do the same here.∎ Wynton Jackson, Knoxville News Sentinel: Iowa State 68, Tennessee 64Iowa State put together a complete performance against a team Tennessee crumbled against twice. The Cyclones showed their top-15 ranked defense with intense ball pressure on Kentucky, keeping the Wildcats out of the paint and draining the shot clock out on the perimeter.Iowa State also forced 20 turnovers in the win, which has been a concern for Tennessee all season. The Vols committed 16 turnovers against Miami (Ohio), and another 10 against Virginia.Kentucky kept pace with the Cyclones in the rebounding battle, which could lean more heavily in Tennessee's favor if Jefferson is out.It is hard, though, to continue banking on elite shooting numbers from the Vols, especially against one of the top defenses in the country. Tennessee also made a number of errors down the stretch that Virginia couldn't capitalize on. Iowa State won't give them the same grace.Blake Toppmeyer: TennesseePaul Myerberg: Iowa StateJordan Mendoza: Iowa StateJohn Brice: Iowa StateMatt Glenesk: TennesseeCraig Meyer: TennesseeJohn Leuzzi: Iowa StateAustin Curtright: Iowa StateEhsan Kassim: TennesseeMoneyline: Iowa State (-190); Tennessee (+154)Spread: Iowa State (-3.5)Over/under total: 139.5Joshua Jefferson injury update: Will Iowa State star play tonight vs Tennessee?Cyclones coach T.J. Otzelberger told reporters in Chicago on Wednesday, March 25 that Iowa State forward Joshua Jefferson has seen "pretty significant progress" with his recovery from an ankle injury and that he is a game-time decision for Friday's Sweet 16 game against 2-seed Tennessee.Jefferson sustained an ankle injury in the opening minutes of the first round of March Madness, and has been sidelined since, including being ruled out in the second round against Kentucky.Jefferson was present at practice and had shed the boot on his ankle on Thursday at the United Center in Chicago.In the 15 minutes the Cyclones practice was open to the media, Jefferson was observed taking practice shots in the first few minutes before spending the majority of the session dribbling near halfcourt and talking to coaches.ESPN's Pete Thamel reported an hour before tip that Jefferson would NOT play Friday night.What did TJ Otzelberger say about UNC basketball coach opening?Ahead of his team's Sweet 16 game against No. 6 seed Tennessee on Friday, March 27, Iowa State coach T.J. Otzelberger started his media availability in Chicago by addressing his name being tied to other job openings.He did not directly mention North Carolina. Here's what he said:"Any speculation with me and any other jobs or opportunities is not true," Otzelberger said on March 25.Nate Ament injury update: How much will Vols star play vs Iowa State?The All-SEC freshman is still dealing with soreness. He played 29 minutes in the Vols' second round win over Virginia, scoring 16 points."There's no chance I'd sit out a March Madness game," he said prior to the UVA game. "It's about what can we do to get back to 100%, or as close to it as we can."Tennessee coach Rick Barnes called the injury a "problem," and Ament won't be fully healthy until he gets time off at the end of the season."We need Nate. He knows it, but he will give us everything that he can, and that's really all I can say about it. If it's up to him, he would play every minute if he could," Barnes said.Rick Barnes March Madness recordBarnes is 37-25 in his career in the NCAA Tournament and led Texas to the 2003 Final Four.Nate Ament 2026 NBA Draft, mock draft predictionNo. 11 overall to Portland Trail Blazers.Kalbrosky's Analysis:After a relatively slow and inefficient start to the season, Tennessee freshman Nate Ament is starting to realize some of his lofty expectations. The freshman averaged 21.6 points per game while shooting 38.9 percent on 3-pointers during a 13-game stretch before an injury against Alabama on Feb. 28. The All-SEC forward then had 27 points (4-of-6 on 3-pointers) with eight rebounds, four assists, three blocks and a steal against Auburn on March 12. It will only take one team to fall in love with Ament and given so much of what he brings to the table cannot be taught, that team is probably picking fairly early in the lottery.See USA TODAY's full mock draft hereNate Ament stats(all stats as of March 15)17.5 points per game6.6 rebounds per game2.5 assists per game40.5% field goal percentage33.1% three-point field goal percentage
